This is something I’ve been thinking about quite a bit while designing my last few MR games.

item.title: Here’s a Unity XR shader tip! 👇
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
Here’s a Unity XR shader tip! 👇
Does your custom shader work in the Editor but render incorrectly in one eye on the headset?
Check its Single-Pass Instanced rendering support!
Make sure you’re using Unity’s stereo macros, including UNITY_VERTEX_OUTPUT_STEREO and UNITY_INITIALIZE_VERTEX_OUTPUT_STEREO.
A great example is shown in this video! The AI agent identified missing stereo macros in my shader. Even though everything looked correct locally, it wasn’t rendering properly on the headset until those fixes were applied.
A good reminder of why testing on the actual device is so important! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2120396165338239472/video/1

item.title: 📣 All, here is another great XR Dev Tip!
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
📣 All, here is another great XR Dev Tip!
I’m adding occlusion to Hand Skate. This concept video compares:
- Static: MRUK wall and ceiling planes are cheaper to draw than dense room meshes
- Dynamic: Meta Depth API for moving objects. Hard edges cost less GPU time, while soft edges look smoother
- Hands: Tracked meshes preserve finger gaps with an extra depth pass
ℹ️ You can use Meta’s Depth API for both static and dynamic occlusion, or combine MRUK room meshes for static surfaces with live depth for moving objects.
The C# component is: EnvironmentDepthManager, under Scripts/EnvironmentDepth in the Meta XR Core SDK (com.meta.xr.sdk.core). Unity 6 OpenXR projects also need the Unity OpenXR Meta package (com.unity.xr.meta-openxr).
In Unity, you can start and stop requesting live depth when mixed reality states change.
depth.enabled = inMR && EnvironmentDepthManager.IsSupported; https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2120344565781614941/video/1

item.title: Here’s a VR rendering technique every XR developer should know about! 👇
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
Here’s a VR rendering technique every XR developer should know about! 👇
Foveated Rendering reduces GPU workload by rendering less detail in your peripheral vision while keeping the important areas sharp.
There are three approaches worth exploring:
• Fixed Foveation: Keeps the center sharp while reducing detail toward the edges. • Eye-Tracked Foveation: Moves the high-detail region wherever your eyes look. • Dynamic Foveation: Adjusts foveation strength based on GPU load.
This is especially interesting for Meta VR Glasses, where eye tracking can help developers optimize rendering without sacrificing detail where players are looking!
In Unity, using Meta XR Core SDK, you can enable fixed and dynamic foveation with:
OVRManager.foveatedRenderingLevel = OVRManager.FoveatedRenderingLevel.High; OVRManager.useDynamicFoveatedRendering = true;
For supported eye-tracking devices:
OVRManager.eyeTrackedFoveatedRenderingSupported OVRManager.eyeTrackedFoveatedRenderingEnabled = true;
Eye-tracked foveation also requires the correct project configuration and eye-tracking permission.
More rendering headroom means more opportunities to create visually impressive VR/MR experiences!
Check out the animation to see how these techniques work! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2120192393039184290/video/1

item.title: Unity XR devs, when would you choose Meta ISDK over Unity XRI + XR Hands? 👇
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
Unity XR devs, when would you choose Meta ISDK over Unity XRI + XR Hands? 👇
Both support many of the same core interactions, including grabbing, poking, rays, and locomotion.
For me, it comes down to the platform, available tools, and how much customization I need.
Unity XRI is great for cross-platform development, while ISDK offers specialized hand interactions and deeper Meta integration.
And remember, ISDK Essentials works with Unity XR Hands too!
💡Curious which one you’re using and why? https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2120118049395089869/video/1

item.title: Here’s a cool MRUK feature worth checking out and a huge time-saver when testing Mixed Reality experiences across a vari
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
Here’s a cool MRUK feature worth checking out and a huge time-saver when testing Mixed Reality experiences across a variety of rooms! 👇
Did you know MRUK has a Spatial Testing framework?
You can automatically run Unity tests across different room prefabs or JSON scenes using RunTestOnAllScenes().
I used this heavily during the development of my game, Fuse Balls, and it helped me catch placement issues early without having to manually test every room configuration! https://x.com/Dilmerv/status/2118131475501420989/video/1

item.title: VR is not dead, nor do I believe I picked the wrong niche.
item.dc:creator: Dilmerv
item.content:encoded:
VR is not dead, nor do I believe I picked the wrong niche. To me, we’re just getting started!
Yes, there are things that haven’t worked well in the past, but without learning from those experiences, how can an ecosystem improve? How can hardware get better?
Focus on the good! I truly believe this next wave of VR/MR devices will shape our future like never before! 🚀
